title: Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park Act of 2017
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on March 15, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park Act of 2017

(Sec. 2) This bill redesignates the Martin Luther King, Junior, National Historic Site in the state of Georgia as the "Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park." The bill replaces the current boundary map with a map of a proposed boundary revision dated June 2015.

summary.headline: A 2018 law renamed the Martin Luther King Jr. National Historic Site in Georgia as a national historical park and replaced its boundary map.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the official name of the Martin Luther King, Junior, National Historic Site in Georgia to the Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park. It also swaps the park's current boundary map for a proposed boundary map dated June 2015. The summary does not say which specific parcels of land are added or removed by the new map.

who_it_affects.how: The site now carries the new park name and is managed under the revised boundary shown on the 2015 map.

who_it_affects.group: National Park Service staff who manage the site
who_it_affects.how: They must follow the new name and the updated boundary map when managing the park.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 8, 2018, and the summary does not list a separate effective date.
